title: InlineForbiddingPositions
description: Issue #142: an inline sub-schema that admits no instance at all, written at every position that resolves rather than names. `items: false` forbids every element and `{"enum":[]}` forbids every value, so the array, map, slot and branch holding one is invalid the moment it holds anything -- and each came out `[]any`, `map[string]any` or a Go type with no check. The two spellings are the same statement, which is why they sit here side by side; the accept-control beside every rejection is the container that holds nothing, which stays valid throughout.

falseItems.$comment: The reported element position. `items: false` forbids every element, so any non-empty array is invalid -- and the empty one is not.

emptyEnumItems.$comment: The same position in the other spelling. enum asserts the instance equals one of the values listed, and there are none.

typedEmptyEnumItems.$comment: A stated type does not rescue an empty enum: no string equals a member of the empty set either. The element used to be typed `string` and accepted every string.

nestedFalseItems.$comment: One level down, where the per-element descent is the only thing that reaches the position. The inner element type was right and its Validate was dispatched by nobody.

nullableFalseItems.$comment: The nullable arm of the same position, which resolveType reaches by a different route. A null is still permitted.

emptyEnumValues.$comment: The reported map-value position: every value is invalid, so an object with any key at all is -- and one with none is not.

nullableEmptyEnumValues.$comment: The nullable spelling of the map, which shares the element tail.

emptyEnumSlot.$comment: A tuple slot, which has answered a `false` position since #126 and read the empty enum as an ordinary sub-schema.

emptyEnumAllOf.$comment: A conjunction with a branch admitting nothing admits nothing, whatever the other branch says.

emptyEnumAnyOf.$comment: A disjunction whose every branch admits nothing admits nothing.

refEmptyEnumAnyOf.$comment: The same branch behind a reference. A $ref is not the schema it names, so the branch has to be resolved before it can be judged -- the rule #116 wrote down for `false` and which the empty enum needs too.

emptyEnumNames.$comment: No property name is admissible, so only the empty object is. Written through a $defs entry because when this was added that was the only spelling `propertyNames` was read in at all -- an inline object property was typed map[string]any and the keyword was dropped there, which #146 closed. The reference stays: it is the position #142 measured, and the inline one is covered by that issue's own fixture.

emptyEnumContains.$comment: `contains` demands at least one matching element and nothing matches, so every array is invalid -- the empty one included, which is what separates this from the positions above.

emptyEnumDependent.$comment: Through a $defs entry for the same reason emptyEnumNames is, and with the same footnote: the inline spelling was typed map[string]any and dropped dependentSchemas whatever the branch said, until #146.

inferredEmptyEnumItems.$comment: The same element position on an array inferred from its keywords rather than declared, which is a separate path through the generator. A string satisfies an items-only schema and must stay valid.

inferredEmptyEnumTail.$comment: The tail of an inferred tuple: in 2020-12 a schema-valued `items` beside prefixItems governs only what follows the prefix, so the first element is free and the second is not.

notEmptyEnum.$comment: The second false-rejection control, and the opposite reading: a `not` over a schema that admits nothing admits everything. The empty enum was read as the empty schema, which made this a forbidden property and refused every document.

notTypedConst.$comment: The same over-reading one keyword along: the inner schema admits the string "x" and nothing else, so the `not` forbids "x" alone. `const` was not read at all and the inner schema was taken for {"type":"string"}, which refused every string there is.

notEmptyEnumBound.$comment: And a third reading of the same inner schema: no value is both at least five and a member of the empty set, so the `not` admits every value.

notAnyOfEmptyEnum.$comment: The branch form a draft-3 `disallow` normalizes to, and the one place a `not` branch is read for its bounds rather than its type alone. The branch admits nothing, so the anyOf does, so the `not` admits everything -- read as if the enum were absent it forbade every number from five up.

notTypedEmptyEnum.$comment: And the empty-enum spelling of it: no string satisfies the inner schema either, so the `not` admits every value.

viaRefFalse.$comment: The control that was already right: the identical element sub-schema behind a $defs entry, which #116 gave the forbidding type in every position. The inline spellings now answer as it does.

viaRefEmptyEnum.$comment: And the empty-enum spelling of that reference, which #121 gave the same type. A $ref is not the schema it names, so the two have to be asked separately.

notEmptyItems.$comment: The working sibling spelling at the element position: `{"not":{}}` is the same empty set and has reached the constraint-only ladder since #126. Its rows must not move.

okEnumItems.$comment: The broad accept-control. An enum that lists values is not the empty one, and a predicate that read len() rather than the nil would forbid every schema in the corpus -- starting here.
